source.title: The Geometry of Refusal: Why Post-Hoc Safety Is Fragile and Pretraining-Time Safety Persists
source.authors: Srikanth Malla; Chi-Ho Choi; J. Choi

record.tranche_reason: The study extends the discussion of post-hoc refusal fragility into pretraining-time safety schedules. It tests whether continuous versus windowed safety co-training changes refusal and its resistance to benign fine-tuning, but does not apply the original difference-in-means direction method.
record.gate_note: The study does not find, ablate, or add a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction. It measures weight-space Fisher geometry and refusal under benign fine-tuning attacks. The reported direction geometry is not a result about the original refusal direction. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: No version is tested. The study never computes, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream direction. It measures weight-space Fisher geometry of safety updates, refusal rates before and after a benign-SFT attack, and how pretraining-time safety schedules affect refusal installation and robustness. V7 concerns whether training decides that one removable direction exists. Refusal robustness to fine-tuning is a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version. Arditi et al. appear only as motivation and related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The authors also conclude that post-hoc safety updates across five families lie nearly orthogonal to capability Fisher directions (a 'suppression' regime). A kernel-immobility lemma, they argue, explains why such updates mask rather than remove capability, hence benign fine-tuning restores it. They also find the features refusal attaches to emerge between 1B and 63B tokens in OLMo-2-1B. Their co-training conclusion, with its stated caveats, is as the record says: persistence not timing; no matched-refusal post-hoc baseline; in-distribution coverage that narrows with scale; single runs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Fisher-eigenspace weight geometry and benign-SFT attack tests, not the original harmful-minus-harmless residual-stream difference direction or its ablation/addition. The co-training experiments compare continuous and windowed safety-loss schedules.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with safety schedule/persistence, pretraining checkpoint, benchmark distribution, model size, and refusal judge. At 1B, regex and classifier readings differ for the co-trained schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: 100 benign Alpaca examples cut regex AdvBench refusal of Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct from 93.0 to 58.2% and Llama-3-8B-Instruct from 49.2 to 10.9%. Classifier scoring shows smaller drops. Mistral has near-zero refusal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc refusal installs are fragile to small benign fine-tuning (fine-tuning-attack fragility, not a direction claim).

fits_no_version.finding: From-scratch safety co-training that persists to the end of pretraining installs 84-98% AdvBench refusal that benign SFT erodes by 2-14 pp (regex) at 410M-6.9B. Llama-Guard scoring shows larger erosion, up to 27 pp at 410M. A windowed schedule of equal total weight installs none. Coverage out of distribution is weak and narrows with scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persistence of a safety loss through pretraining, not its timing, yields refusal robust to benign fine-tuning (in-distribution).

fits_no_version.finding: An SFT+DPO install on OLMo-2-1B checkpoints yields measurable refusal only at 1B and 4001B tokens. The attack collapses it (21.9→0%, 42.2→15.6%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness of post-hoc refusal depends on the base's pretraining stage.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful-minus-benign hidden-state divergence between base and instruct is layer-localized (peaks: Qwen block 24, Llama 12, Mistral 13). On OLMo-2-1B it emerges between 1B and 63B pretraining tokens. This is a distance measure, not the mean-difference direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representations a refusal install engages emerge in a sharp pretraining transition.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says the full code is in supplementary material and refers to an anonymized repository, without giving a URL.
record.problems: The paper does not test the claimed single direction or its ablation. The post-hoc comparison at 410M has no matched-refusal baseline because its DPO recipe installs no measurable refusal. Co-training conditions are single runs; the authors note data-loading issues in earlier runs. Refusal scoring differs between regex and classifier, and out-of-distribution refusal is weaker. The geometry instrument uses a top-k Fisher eigenspace and omits tail directions.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the 160M pilot (Appendix K, Table 24), additional detector results for HarmBench and StrongReject (Appendix L, Tables 25–27), and capability NLL outcomes (Appendix K, Table 20); these were not needed for the schedule/refusal rows and the 60-row limit prioritizes direct refusal outcomes and differing conditions. Also omitted geometric measurements that do not measure a claimed refusal direction.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is found, ablated or added; no capability check of such an ablation.
No abliteration or weight edit from a direction.
The benign-SFT attack is applied, but no test of whether it suppresses the direction; no training against direction ablation.
No single-direction vs. multi-direction, cone or affine comparison.
No separation of harmfulness representation from refusal decision.
No transfer of a direction across languages, variants or base/instruct.
Safety schedules are varied, but whether they decide the existence of one removable direction is never measured; only refusal rate and robustness to benign SFT.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked V7 as tested. However, V7 is about whether one removable direction exists, and no row measures a direction, so all rows are relinked to none and no verdicts are given. R57/R58 duplicate R41/R42. The early co-training runs (R10-R16) predate a data-loader fix. Regex and classifier readings diverge substantially for co-trained models. The 160M pilot and stronger-attack sweep (Table 23) are omitted, but they bear on no version either.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction is found or causally ablated/added; no test of whether such an ablation preserves general capability.
No direction ablation is converted into a weight edit or tested as an abliteration procedure.
The study applies benign supervised fine-tuning attacks, but does not test whether attacks suppress the claimed direction or whether training against that direction's ablation improves robustness.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test of the claimed direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.

Tests how safety-training schedules affect refusal installation and resistance to benign fine-tuning, but does not test whether those schedules determine the existence of a single removable refusal direction.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Continuous or post-substrate co-training that persists to the end; AdvBench refusal
reader_labels.reason: Continuous schedules retain high AdvBench refusal after benign-SFT across the reported scales and schedules, unlike the early window; see R10, R13–R14, R17–R20 and R45–R47.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Windowed schedules, out-of-distribution prompts, and classifier scoring
reader_labels.reason: The equal-total-weight windowed schedule installs little or no refusal; out-of-distribution refusal is lower and can erode substantially, and classifier scoring reports more erosion than regex on several conditions; see R11, R15, R21–R28, R41–R44 and R50–R52.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Post-hoc instruct models under benign-SFT attack
reader_labels.reason: The attack substantially lowers refusal on Qwen and Llama, while Mistral has little baseline refusal to lose; the measured rates also depend on detector, see R01–R09 and R54–R56.
